items.text: Thank you for your ongoing support of SPRAWL zero. We have been hard at work going through your feedback and working on this new patch, which is available on all platforms (except for Nintendo Switch and Epic, which I promise are coming soon!).
Please take a look at the Patch Notes below of the new fixes!
Fixed an issue where explosives taking damage while held would detonate upon reload after being dropped.
Fixed an issue where the Hitokiri would parry itself and other dropped weapons.
Reduced enemy density for select NG+ exclusive encounters.
Added additional New York Minute time extenders.
Fixed an issue where SIX would occasionally fail to spawn.
Fixed an edge case causing players carrying a turret to teleport incorrectly in NG+.
Fixed an issue where the player could get stuck inside the first lift.
Fixed an issue in NG+ where Junta enemies would attack prematurely.
Fixed an edge case where the exit subway gate would fail to open.
Added a flashlight trigger in a key dark area.
Fixed an issue where Laeta's dialogue could overlap.
Shogun now joins the street brawl encounter on NG+.
Fixed NPC cleanup issues when sequence breaking.
Moved a Relic Fragment to a nearby alternative location.
Polished scripting during the final arena encounter.
Fixed an issue causing Tsuchigumo to not properly return to its resting state.
Fixed an issue where Laeta's dialogue could overlap.
Fixed an edge case where the first quest was assigned too late.
Fixed an issue that could cause the final boss to not die while the One Shot Relic was enabled.
Fixed an issue where enemies would not die from Burn or Shock damage while the One Shot Relic was enabled.
Fixed an issue where the Spartan Golden Relic failed to properly disable sprint.
Addict Relic effect now correctly pauses during a key narrative scene in NG+.
Fixed an issue that caused relics to not properly activate upon defeating the final boss on NG+

We hope you continue enjoying your time with SPRAWL zero, and please continue to let us know of any bugs you come across and feedback you may have - it really helps us to continue to make SPRAWL zero the best it can be!

I just want to open by saying a massive thank you to all of you for playing SPRAWL zero. Seeing such an overwhelmingly positive response to our game has been completely surreal. We’re a tiny indie team of just four people who set out to build a game we genuinely wanted to play, and all the love has made the journey worthwhile.

One thing we pride ourselves on is that we actually listen. We’ve been keeping a close eye on your feedback, watching streams, and reading community posts. For the past two weeks, we’ve been working nonstop on a massive patch that addresses the biggest requests, balance tweaks, and bugs present in the game. In total, this update packs 183 updates, and I’d love to take a moment to highlight some of the key changes.

Many players reported that Rushdown felt inconsistent or clunky to use, leading some to think the ability was flat-out broken. This created a nasty downstream issue: players stopped using Rushdown in the second half of the game, where shielded enemies become much more common. Since Rushdown instantly strips shields, ignoring it could turn the late game into a slog against bullet sponge enemies.
We heard you loud and clear and made several core changes to make Rushdown feel awesome:
Manual Activation & Freedom of Movement: You no longer need to be moving to activate Rushdown, and you can now manually trigger a punch even without a lunge target. Less misfires, more control.
Adrenaline Economy: Adrenaline no longer drains until Rushdown is fully charged, significantly lowering the cost to use it.
Clarity: We’ve improved the tutorial, and added a reminder prompt in Eden clarifying that Rushdown disables shields.

The Rushdown adjustments naturally tied into broader balance issues in the second half of SPRAWL zero, so we didn't stop there. From Eden onward, we’ve made extensive balance passes to dramatically smooth out the experience:
Roster Adjustments: Shielded enemies are less dense in late-game encounters, reducing combat friction.

Weapon Buffs: Late-game weapons across the board have received substantial buffs (e.g., Vox Dei ammo boosted to 200, Rocket Launcher damage bumped from 400 to 1000 with shield-stripping capabilities).
Throwable Damage Scaling: Thrown weapons now deal damage based on their rarity tier, meaning you can more reliably kill enemies with thrown weapons throughout the game.
Telegraphing & Cues: Junta Helicopters now display clear on screen lock on indicators and distinct incoming missile audio warnings.
The second half of SPRAWL zero will still test your skill, but it will feel like a fair challenge rather than an overwhelming difficulty spike.
Although performance has been widely praised across most setups, we identified key areas where lower-end hardware and specific configurations struggled.

notes.title: We’ve rolled out major optimizations across the entire game

items.text: Particle Overhaul: Every single particle effect has been optimized with zero loss in visual quality, and in many cases, improved visual fidelity.
Graphics Optimizations: Sky materials, breakable objects, and heavy sequence lighting have been streamlined to boost frame rates.

Steam Deck Preset: We’ve added a dedicated "Optimize for Steam Deck" preset button in the settings menu. If your hardware meets Steam Deck specs, hitting this button will get you running at a smooth, locked 60 FPS.
This was one of our most requested features, and I’m super happy to announce that you can now stack all Golden Relics simultaneously!

Have fun running around with infinite Hitokiri ammo while your enemies sport oversized heads and explode into cheerful confetti, or activate any other crazy combination you want. It feels like a proper, chaotic reward for completing those tough relic challenges in New Game+.
A significant portion of player feedback centered on the final boss encounter. We took a hard look at the fight to make it feel much fairer, more interactive, and far less punishing when you fail:

Fairer Attacks & Telegraphing: We slowed down the Final Boss laser attack animation speed by 20% and reduced its explosive damage by 25%. We also added clear attack notify flares and muzzle flashes for both his minigun and laser attacks.

Better Attack Sequencing: The boss will now perform his Somatic Amber attack following Astra Dei (instead of jumping straight into a laser), and we've added a longer delay before he initiates new attacks.

Interactive Mechanics: You can now use the Manus Dei to catch and throw back the massive rocks the Final Boss hurls at you. If he catches you in a grab attack, you can now mash buttons to break free in addition to the interact prompt.

Pacing & Checkpoints: The Final Boss’ carapace now stays open during Phase 1 to keep damage windows readable. Most importantly, we’ve added opening dialogue checkpoints and new checkpoints right before the Condemned phase in each stage, so a quick mistake won't cost you minutes of set-up time.
Bug Fixes: Fixed critical bugs where Astra Dei projectiles phased through shields and geometry, as well as edge cases where the Final Boss would zip into the sky or walk out of the arena bounds.
We’ve been reading through all your feature requests, and this update brings a suite of long-awaited quality-of-life additions and settings:
Retro Mode: A brand new retro visual presentation for players looking for a classic CRT aesthetic overhaul.
Collectibles Tracker: Easily track your missing items directly from the pause menu.
Expanded Photomode: Added AutoFocus support with smart object detection, "FIVE" and "MAETH" borders, and automatic hiding of low health, burn, shock, and poison screen overlays while taking shots.
Granular Gameplay Toggles: You can now toggle off Aim Assist, Hitmarkers, Crosshairs, Enemy Healthbars, or Reduce Screen Effects.

Expanded Display & Controls: FOV slider cap increased to 140 with Viewmodel FOV controls, increased mouse sensitivity precision, SMAA support in menus, and Invert Look settings moved out of the Gamepad submenu so mouse users can access them directly.

notes.title: Thank you all again for the unbelievable support, feedback, and passion you’ve shown for SPRAWL zero. Jump into the update, give the new settings and balance changes a spin, and let us know what you think!

notes.title: First off, thank you all so much for playing the SPRAWL Zero demo!

items.text: It’s been incredible to see nearly everyone loving it. We’ve been reading every comment, watching every clip, and taking all the positivity in. Thank you for playing and for sharing your thoughts on our Discord, Steam, and socials.

As promised, we’ve taken your feedback to heart. We are stoked to announce that you can now hop into an updated demo featuring plenty of the great changes you’ve been asking for, plus a brand-new weapon!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46009351/6eb322ce9ca71ccbb2216e68ad15f93f0ebb7210.png"]
Reworked Mantling System

We heard you: mantling onto surfaces felt a bit off. I’m happy to announce the entire system has been reworked from top to bottom and should feel much better. That being said, it’s still a work in progress! Some of our craftier players might find a few edge cases, but we’re actively smoothing those out to ensure it feels perfect for the full launch.
Difficulty Adjustments

The demo includes the first two levels of the game, which serve as an introduction to our mechanics and world. By design, these are the easiest levels. However, we agree the game felt a bit too easy, especially for players selecting Martyr (our hardest difficulty). We've made adjustments across the board: Martyr should now produce a significant challenge even in the early game, and Normal will give players a tougher test of skill.
Performance Improvements

For this demo, we opted to give players access to a development build. This allows you to share detailed logs and access the dev console in the event of major issues (which, thankfully, we haven’t really had!). Because it's a dev build, it runs about 20% less performant than a final shipping build will.

However, we’ve made changes that should translate into notable performance improvements for nearly everyone; up to 90 FPS in some cases! Performance will continue to improve as we keep working on the game.
For players running on maxed-out settings, we recommend turning everything down to Medium, and then back up to Max for these new performance boosts to fully take effect.
New Weapon Added: The Vox Dei

This is just for fun, but since we are updating the game, we figured why not give you all the chance to use a new weapon? The Vox Dei; a devastating Imago Dei Minigun, has been added to all gold crates. Have fun finding it!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46009351/d3f49573de511cc84594edeabd49bd7f4dafe071.png"]
Weapon Balance & Projectile Grabbing
Weapon Roles: We’ve tweaked several weapons and adjusted their tiers to properly reflect their roles. The Vulcan, for example, is now a Blue rarity weapon.
Projectile Grabbing: Grabbing fireballs and Impaler shots will now electrify them! This is hard to pull off, so we felt it should be more rewarding.
Objective Navigation & Briefings

Navigation: When gaining a new objective (or pressing ALT to bring it back up), the marker should no longer feel obtuse or bounce around. We've made changes to significantly improve navigating the SPRAWL.
Mission Briefings: These have received some polish and updated content to better introduce players to game mechanics.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46009351/50e417d43212fbf87bf184a62ca48182b5604ee0.png"]

General QOL: Every map has received multiple bug fixes (major and minor). We've also improved enemy navigation and player geometry, meaning explorers have less of a chance of getting stuck or accidentally teleported (whoops)! You’ll also notice some nice visual eye-candy changes.
Fixed Settings menu issues.
Improved vault fluidity and responsiveness.
Lowered health of explosives.

Added new content to level briefing screens and fixed focus issues.
Fixed an issue causing the Gavel to miss often when aiming down sights (ADS).

Made allied AI spread out more when following the player.

Made relic fragments and codex pickups unable to be dropped by performing ADS while grabbing.
Enemies that are burning to death will stand up less often now.
Poison buildup is now faster, and poison deals damage properly when activated.
Weapons now play a special sound when breaking on an enemy.
"Hide reminders" option should now work as intended.
Added coyote time.
Enemies killed by an adrenaline ability now drop 1 health stim, down from 3.
AI should now prioritize nearby targets more often.
Fixed issues that could cause the ADS state to persist between weapons.z
Sightless Sisters now drop their sickles
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46009351/b43943b117c46d530ac99252977177eb64d3ef0b.gif"]
As a thank you to everyone playing the demo, we wanted to do something fun for our community. We’re giving away a couple of $25 Steam Gift Cards and game codes for the first SPRAWL!

items.text: OR share one of your demo gameplay clips with us on our socials!

We’re a tiny indie team working non-stop, through long days and deep into the night. We’re building SPRAWL Zero to be the best it can possibly be. This game pays homage to an era we hold incredibly close to us, and we know it is important to so many of you too. It makes us so happy to know that even this early, it's sticking the landing for so many of you.
We hope you have a blast playing, and we look forward to hearing your thoughts as we gather feedback for our next steps!
Found a bug? Please report it using our Discord channels.
Show us what you can do! We want to see your most awesome gameplay clips. Share them with the community!
